questions.question:

Any declarations or practices of religious __antipathy__ against ethnic minorities in a democratic country should not be tolerated.

__
 
• The word **"antipathy"** means a deep-seated feeling of dislike; aversion. (घृणा)

• **"Enmity"** refers to a state of active opposition or hostility. (शत्रुता)

• **Example: **The **devaluation **of the currency caused economic instability.

• **Example:** The company's **conformity **to industry regulations ensured its credibility.

questions.question: Select the grammatically correct sentence.

options.text: An intrepid explorer stumbled upon an uncharted cavern deep within the heart of the rainforest.
The intrepid explorer stumbled upon the uncharted cavern deep within the heart of the rainforest.
An intrepid explorer stumbled upon the uncharted cavern deep within a heart of the rainforest.
The intrepid explorer stumbled upon an uncharted cavern deep within a heart of the rainforest.

questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**To arrive at the correct answer, let's re-evaluate each sentence with a focus on why option 1 might be considered the most fitting:**

__
 
• **1) An intrepid explorer stumbled upon an uncharted cavern deep within the heart of the rainforest.**

 
 
• This sentence uses the indefinite article "an" before "intrepid explorer," introducing a non-specific explorer. This is perfectly grammatically correct and natural when the explorer is being introduced for the first time or is not a specific individual known to the context.
 
• The phrase "the heart of the rainforest" is the correct idiomatic expression for the central region.
 
• This sentence is grammatically and contextually sound__.
 
 
 
• **2) The intrepid explorer stumbled upon the uncharted cavern deep within the heart of the rainforest.**
 
 
• This sentence uses the definite article "the," which typically implies a specific explorer known to the context. Without prior mention of this explorer, "an" (as in option 1) might be considered more appropriate for an initial introduction of the subject.
 
 
 
• **3) An intrepid explorer stumbled upon the uncharted cavern deep within a heart of the rainforest.**
 
 
• This sentence is grammatically incorrect. "A heart of the rainforest" is not the standard phrasing; it should be "the heart."
 
 
 
• **4) The intrepid explorer stumbled upon the uncharted cavern deep within a heart of the rainforest.**
 
 
• This sentence is also grammatically incorrect due to the use of "a heart" instead of "the heart."
 
 

**Considering the nuances of article usage, especially when introducing a subject without prior context, the indefinite article "an" in option 1 is a natural and grammatically correct choice. It introduces the explorer as a general entity within the narrative.**

**Therefore, based on this analysis:**

**The correct answer is option 1.**

questions.question:
Read the sentence given below and identify if there is an error in it. The error can be in any segment of the sentence which are marked A, B, C, and D. Select option D if there is 'No error'.

(A) She sings / (B) the song / (C) beautiful in the party / (D) No error.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in segment (C) of the sentence: "**beautiful in the party**."
 
• The word "**beautiful**" is an adjective, and in this context, an adverb is needed to modify the verb "sings." The correct adverbial form is "**beautifully**."
 
• Additionally, the preposition should be "**at**" when referring to being present at an event like a party, not "in."
 
• Therefore, segment (C) should be "**beautifully at the party**."

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"She sings **the song beautifully at the party**."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **(A) She sings** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct. "Sings" is the correct verb form for the third-person singular subject "She."
 
• **(B) the song** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct. "Song" is a noun, and "the" is the definite article correctly preceding it.
 
• **(D) No error** – This option is incorrect because there is a grammatical error in segment (C).
 
• Using the correct adverb ("beautifully") to modify the verb and the correct preposition ("at") to indicate location are crucial for grammatical accuracy.

questions.question: Select the grammatically correct sentence.

options.text: The traffic on a highway was heavy during an evening.
The traffic on the highway was heavy during the evening.
The traffic on the highway was heavy during an evening.
A traffic on the highway was heavy during an evening.

questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**Let's analyze each sentence to determine the grammatically correct option:**

__
 
• **1) The traffic on a highway was heavy during an evening.**

 
 
• While "a highway" is grammatically correct, "an evening" is less natural. We usually refer to a specific part of the day with "the" when it's implied or understood.
 
 
 
• **2) The traffic on the highway was heavy during the evening.**
 
 
• "The traffic" is appropriate as traffic is generally considered a singular mass noun in this context. "The highway" implies a specific highway, which is natural. "During the evening" is the standard and grammatically correct way to refer to that part of the day.
 
• This sentence is grammatically and contextually correct__.
 
 
 
• **3) The traffic on the highway was heavy during an evening.**
 
 
• Similar to option 1, "an evening" is less natural than "the evening."
 
 
 
• **4) A traffic on the highway was heavy during an evening.**
 
 
• "Traffic" is generally an uncountable noun, so it doesn't typically take the indefinite article "a." We say "heavy traffic," not "a traffic." Also, "an evening" is less natural.
 
 

**Based on the analysis, option 2 uses the articles "the" appropriately for both "traffic," "highway," and "evening" in this context.**

**Therefore, the grammatically correct sentence is:**

**The traffic on the highway was heavy during the evening.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The future perfect tense is used to describe an action that will be completed before a specific time in the future.
 
• The structure of the future perfect tense is: **will/shall + have + past participle**.
 
• In the given sentence, the action of washing all the clothes is expected to be completed before the action of coming into the house again.
 
• Option 1, "I hope you will have washed all the clothes before you come into the house again," correctly uses the future perfect tense ("will have washed") for the first action.

Therefore, the correct answer is **1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"I hope you **will have washed** all the clothes before you come into the house again."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **2) I hope you shall wash all the clothes before you come into the house again.** – This option uses the simple future tense ("shall wash"), not the future perfect. While "shall" can be used for the future, "will" is more common in modern English for most subjects.
 
• **3) I hope you will be washing all the clothes before you come into the house again.** – This option uses the future continuous tense ("will be washing"), which describes an ongoing action in the future, not a completed one before another future action.
 
• **4) I hope you will have wash all the clothes before you come into the house again.** – This option incorrectly uses the base form of the verb "wash" after "will have." The past participle ("washed") is required for the future perfect tense.

• The error in the sentence lies in the use of the double superlative "**most beautifulest**."
 
• Superlatives are used to indicate the highest degree of a quality, and typically, only one form (either "most" + adjective or adjective + "-est") should be used.

• **4) art class today!** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not contain the error.
 
• Using double superlatives like "most beautifulest" is a common grammatical mistake. It's important to use either the "most + adjective" form or the "adjective + -est" form, but not both together.
